rule.text: - Break a large render into focused render methods named for purposeful semantic regions.

- Do not use inline event callbacks. Pass named handler references to event props. Define and bind handlers outside render; do not place arrow functions, function expressions, or `.bind(...)` calls in JSX event props or event props inside JSX spreads and input/slot property objects. Render-prop and list-mapping callbacks are not event callbacks. Static checking covers syntactically visible event values; reviewers trace aliases and callback factories that require reasoning.
- Components do not reach directly into models, transport logic, or unrelated registry services.

| Owner | Must own | Must not own |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Registry | app-facing service lookup, lifecycle coordination, and event surfaces | feature policy, startup selection, or domain behavior |
| Executor | startup sequencing and initial controller/flow selection from external facts | page workflow, presentation, domain rules, or an implicit first-page policy |
| Model | canonical durable/domain state, transport, persistence, serialization, normalization, and reusable domain rules | JSX, layout, localized labels, navigation, or screen workflow |
| App-facing service | a stable capability, lifecycle, caching, subscriptions, and adaptation over models/internal collaborators | screen-specific presentation or another owner's policy |
| Controller | commands, user-facing workflow, orchestration, feature sessions, activation/mounting, and invalidation | JSX, CSS, DOM mechanics, raw storage/transport, or duplicated canonical state |
| View service | projection of controller state/actions into presentation-ready values, component choice, mounting, and event relay | domain mutation, persistence, transport, routing policy, defaults, or independent workflow |
| React presentation | semantic JSX, MUI/DOM interaction, rendering, and genuinely transient visual state | registry orchestration, model/service calls, durable mutation, URL parsing, or feature mounting |

Everything beneath a feature is private by default. Another feature must not
import its controller, view, component, model, helper, CSS, type declaration,
test support, or asset. Cross-feature collaboration must use one of these
intentional seams:
Feature-internal code and assets are private. When another feature needs a capability, expose a narrow service or promote a genuinely shared building block instead of importing feature internals.

`index.js` is the feature's runtime activation boundary. Keep most
feature-crossing imports there: it imports the owned implementations that
register services and contributions. Consumers locate app-facing capabilities
through the registry. A feature view may directly import its own concrete React
tree and private presentation helpers; that exception does not make those files
public to other features.

Services may start in parallel. Registry presence is not proof of readiness. Cross-service behavior belongs in `ready()` and every listener/resource requires matching cleanup.
- do not call other services or assume their initialization is complete.
Every owned subscription, listener, timer, observer, connection, and imperative resource needs precise, idempotent cleanup. Replacing a transport or remounting a view must not accumulate listeners.

The application entry imports Polylith's generated feature aggregate so included feature entrypoints execute. Build-generated configuration and loadables likewise remain declared build concerns. Do not replace those seams with a manually maintained list of feature implementation imports.

entries.reason: The render method contains several distinct header, filtering, results, detail, and footer regions without focused render methods.
entries.consequence: The large render obscures semantic regions and their maintenance boundaries.
entries.remedy: Extract named render methods for the header, filters, results, details, and footer.

entries.reason: The click prop receives an inline arrow callback.
entries.consequence: A new event callback is created during each render.
entries.remedy: Bind a named refresh handler outside render and pass it to onClick.

entries.reason: The component directly performs transport access with fetch.
entries.consequence: Presentation owns transport work that belongs behind a model or service boundary.
entries.remedy: Receive orders and a refresh callback through the owning view/controller boundary.

entries.reason: React presentation performs direct transport work, which the responsibility matrix prohibits.
entries.consequence: The React layer bypasses the model/service and controller workflow boundaries.
entries.remedy: Move loading to the owning controller and service/model; pass presentation values and actions to React.

entries.reason: This file defines a view service and contains no React render method.
This file contains no JSX event props.
This file is not a React component.
The view service chooses workflow state and directly mutates through its model, both reserved for the controller/model boundary.
entries.consequence: Workflow policy and domain mutation are embedded in presentation coordination.
entries.remedy: Have the view relay submit intent to its controller, which owns the decision and model/service call.

entries.reason: This controller file contains no React render method.
This file contains no JSX event props.
This file is not a React component.
The controller directly uses raw browser persistence, which the matrix assigns to the model layer.
entries.consequence: Persistence bypasses the model/service boundary and becomes coupled to page workflow.
entries.remedy: Move persistence to an owning model or service and have the controller invoke its stable contract.

entries.reason: The small component has one focused button render region.
The event prop receives a named handler bound outside render.
The component relays user intent through an owner-supplied callback and has no direct model, transport, or registry access.
The React component renders a control and reports intent through its supplied callback.
The orders controller reaches billing's private implementation through a shared re-export, which does not create an intentional cross-feature seam.

evidence.quote: // Billing feature's private implementation; not a published feature entry.

entries.consequence: Orders depends on billing internals and billing cannot be removed or changed independently.
entries.remedy: Expose billing through an app-facing registry service or documented public feature contract.

entries.reason: The controller consumes billing's feature-private implementation via a re-export instead of a narrow service or shared building block.

evidence.quote: // Billing feature's private implementation; not a published feature entry.

entries.consequence: Feature privacy is bypassed and cross-feature capability ownership is hidden.
entries.remedy: Register a narrow billing capability and resolve it through the registry.

entries.reason: The controller crosses feature ownership through a direct implementation import rather than locating an app-facing capability through the registry.

evidence.quote: // Billing feature's private implementation; not a published feature entry.

entries.consequence: Feature-crossing ownership is hidden outside the activation and registry seam.
entries.remedy: Use a registry-provided billing capability from the controller.

entries.reason: The orders controller obtains billing through a registry capability rather than importing feature internals.
The cross-feature dependency uses a narrow registry service seam.
The consumer locates the app-facing billing capability through the registry.
Cross-service resolution, refresh, and listener installation occur in start, and the listener has no matching cleanup.
entries.consequence: Parallel startup can observe an unready dependency and repeated lifecycle use accumulates listeners.
entries.remedy: Move dependency work to ready, retain the listener reference, and remove it during idempotent cleanup.

entries.reason: start calls another registry service before dependency readiness is established.
entries.consequence: The service assumes dependency initialization during the parallel start phase.
entries.remedy: Resolve and use the dependency in ready.

entries.reason: The owned changed listener is installed but stop provides no cleanup.
entries.consequence: Restarting the service can retain stale listeners and duplicate recalculation.
entries.remedy: Store a listener reference and unregister it in idempotent cleanup.

entries.reason: Local state initializes in start; cross-service work occurs in ready and is cleaned up in stop.
start initializes only local state and does not access other services.
The retained listener is removed during guarded cleanup.
The application entry manually imports a feature implementation instead of the generated feature aggregate.
entries.consequence: Activation no longer follows build-selected feature aggregation.

entries.reason: The main entry directly imports a feature implementation rather than the generated feature aggregate.
entries.consequence: Feature activation bypasses the build and side-effect entry boundary.
entries.remedy: Replace the direct implementation import with the generated feature aggregate import.

entries.reason: The application entry imports the generated Polylith feature aggregate.
The main entry uses the generated feature aggregate rather than an individual feature implementation.
